newsitem.title: USA: 18 men charged in federal stock conspiracy.
newsitem.headline: 18 men charged in federal stock conspiracy.

text.p: Grand jurors have indicted 18 men on federal conspiracy charges resulting from an FBI investigation of bribes made to stockbrokers in sales of Nasdaq and over-the-counter stocks, officials said Wednesday.

In one of two cases announced Wednesday, 12 of the 18 were charged with conspiracy to commit wire fraud and bribery following an FBI sting in which agents posed as corrupt brokers willing to accept bribes.

Defendants were accused of conspiring to manipulate the price of the common stock of Spaceplex Amusement Centres International LTD, a Nevada-based corporation that owned and operated an amusement park in St. James, N.Y., east of New York City.

In the other case, six other men were charged with a conspiracy to give and accept secret payments to securities brokers in order to induce the brokers to cause their clients to buy stock in San Diego Bancorp Inc., a California-based manufacturer of environmentally friendly products, the government said.
The indictment in the first case was filed in federal court last Thursday. The second indictment was filed Monday.
Among the 12 defendants in the Spaceplex case were Joseph Pignatiello, 50, of Coral Springs, Fla.; John Fasano, 37, of Hauppauge, N.Y. and James Manas, 44, of Belle Harbour, N.Y.
Manas is president of Spaceplex, and Pignatiello and Fasano were stock promoters in the venture, a prosecutors' spokesman said.

According to the indictments, Pignatiello, Fasano, Manas and the other defendants made unlawful secret payments to an undercover agent posing as securities broker in order to induce him to cause his customers to make a series of Spaceplex common stock purchases intended to raise the stock's price.
If convicted, the defendants each face prison terms of between five and 20 years in prison and substantial fines.
